Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Advanced degree in education, public policy, social science, statistics, higher education administration, or a related field involving quantitative or policy analysis.
Demonstrated experience extracting, integrating, validating, analyzing, and interpreting data from multiple systems or data sources.
Experience in higher education academic planning, curriculum planning, enrollment management, student success analysis, institutional research, or resource planning.
Demonstrated experience preparing dashboards, visualizations, presentations, briefing materials, reports, or executive-level summaries for leadership decision-making.
Experience with curriculum and leave planning, instructional workload analysis, instructional support budgeting, external reviews, program review, or academic program development.

Experience using spreadsheet, presentation, collaboration, reporting, project tracking, and data visualization tools such as Excel, Google Sheets, Google Slides, PowerPoint, Google Workspace, and dashboard/reporting tools.
Experience working with vendors, data management teams, or system implementation teams to improve functionality, data integration, reporting, exports, documentation, and user workflows.
Experience using AI-enabled productivity or analytical tools to support drafting, synthesis, analysis, workflow improvement, presentation development, or project coordination.
Experience creating dashboards or data visualizations using tools such as Tableau, Looker Studio, Power BI, Excel, Google Sheets, or similar platforms.
Experience using generative AI tools to support research synthesis, drafting, process documentation, data interpretation, workflow design, or presentation development.
Experience working with student success, advising, retention, persistence, graduation, gateway course, placement, or academic progress data.
Experience managing operational budgets, tracking commitments, preparing financial summaries, or supporting budget planning processes.
Experience supporting senior leadership through meeting preparation, correspondence drafting, agenda coordination, follow-up tracking, and executive-level project support.
Experience maintaining Google Groups, shared communication lists, message trackers, or internal communications workflows.

Under the direction of the Assistant Dean/Chief of Staff, the Senior Analyst, Academic Planning and Resources provides high-level analytical, operational, systems, and project leadership for the Division of Physical & Biological Sciences. The position supports divisional decision-making in academic planning, curriculum and leave planning, instructional workload, enrollment capacity, teaching assistant (TA) and instructional support budget planning, student success analysis, external reviews, resource planning, dean's office operations, and campus reporting. The Senior Analyst independently extracts, integrates, validates, analyzes, and interprets data from multiple campus and divisional sources and translates findings into dashboards, presentations, briefing materials, correspondence drafts, implementation trackers, and decision-support summaries for the Dean, Assistant Deans, Associate Deans, Department Chairs, managers, and campus partners. The incumbent serves as a divisional subject-matter expert on academic planning systems, curriculum and workload data, instructional support and TA budget planning tools, catalog and scheduling processes, student success reporting, and operational coordination for recurring leadership cycles. The role requires advanced judgment, discretion, initiative, and the ability to convert complex data, policy, and process issues into clear options and recommendations for senior leadership.
Familiarity with UC Santa Cruz systems, policies, academic governance, curriculum processes, catalog/scheduling systems, advising systems, and divisional operations.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate has the option to work a hybrid work schedule. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills sufficient to analyze complex data, policies, processes, and written materials; identify issues; develop options; and make recommendations.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple complex projects, deadlines, stakeholders, and recurring operational cycles.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, set priorities, and move work forward with limited direction.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft correspondence, summaries, reports, presentations, and executive-level materials.

Ability to use emerging technologies responsibly, including understanding when AI-enabled tools are appropriate and when confidential, protected, sensitive, or non-public data must not be entered into unapproved systems.
Ability to work with discretion and maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive personnel, student, salary, financial, academic, strategic, or non-public information.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, managers, department leadership, campus partners, vendors, and senior administrators.
